what_happened: Planning read found that the module docstring claim 'hmarkers holds at colourFibre D for every D' is false as literally stated: hmarkers quantifies over ALL TaskModels of the frame, and a valuation making markerAtom false everywhere refutes it. The claim is true only under the intended marker valuation. The plan therefore adds a fixed-model variant of the reduction theorem plus a markerModel definition, and requires correcting two docstrings, rather than discharging the existing all-models hypothesis.

Task description names 'the probes/ file' as the consumer, but the probe content has since landed in FormalSystem/Metalogic/Independence/OpenFutureUndefinable.lean and specs/ROADMAP.md line 228 directs re-pointing scope at the landed module. Plan targets the landed module and declares the 859 probe out of scope.

The 'instance-unification blocker' turned out to be a one-line asymmetry found in minutes: FrameOver.translationProduct states its own @[simp] _taskRel bridge in the same file, colourClock does not. No research dispatch was needed; targeted reads of TranslationProduct.lean, TaskFrame.lean and PartialHistory.lean grounded the whole plan.

colourClock_taskRel closed on the first rung of the plan's mitigation ladder: a bare 'FrameOver.ofReflectiveRegular_taskRel' term, with no haveI, no show, and no reflect_restrict_iff fallback. The Nonempty (W x D) instance baked into colourClock's body unified with the lemma's instance-implicit argument by postponed instance unification, exactly as translationProduct_taskRel already does.

git-commit-scoped.sh refused the phase-1 commit on typst-sync-check.sh Check 2: typst/generated/status.typ's formalsystem-line-count was 15 lines stale, exactly the size of this phase's edit. Fixed forward with 'bash scripts/typst-sync-check.sh --fix' and added typst/generated/status.typ to the phase's staged path list. Consequence for later phases: every Lean-line-count-changing phase in this plan must regenerate and stage that file, which the plan's Files-to-modify lists do not name.
